sentences.zh: 朱克融朱克融，賊泚之從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong — Zhu Kerong was the grandnephew of the rebel Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong was a grandnephew of the rebel Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 祖滔，父洄。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Zhu Tao; his father was Zhu Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Zhu Tao, and his father was Zhu Hui.

sentences.zh: 克融少為幽州軍校，事節度使劉總。

translations.literal: Kerong in his youth was an officer in the Youzhou army and served Military Governor Liu Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Kerong served as an officer in the Youzhou army under Military Governor Liu Zong.

sentences.zh: 總將歸朝，慮其有變，籍軍中素有異志者，薦之闕下，時克融亦在籍中。

translations.literal: When Zong was about to return to court, fearing trouble he registered men in the army who had long harbored disloyal designs and recommended them to the capital; at that time Kerong was also on the register.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong was preparing to return to court, fearing unrest he registered soldiers who had long harbored disloyal ambitions and sent their names to the capital; Kerong was among those listed.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔植、杜元穎不知兵，且無遠略，謂兩河無虞，遂奏勒歸鎮。

translations.literal: The Chief Ministers Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of military affairs and had no long-range vision; believing the two Hebei circuits secure, they memorialized that these men be ordered back to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ministers Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of warfare and lacked long-range vision; assuming the two Hebei circuits were secure, they memorialized that the men be sent back to their commands.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，幽州軍亂，囚其帥張弘靖。

translations.literal: In the early Changqing era the Youzhou army mutinied and imprisoned its commander Zhang Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing reign the Youzhou army mutinied and imprisoned its commander Zhang Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 時洄廢疾於家，軍中素伏其謀略，至是眾欲立之。

translations.literal: At that time Hui lay ill at home; the troops had long respected his stratagems, and now the multitude wished to install him as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was then laid up at home with illness; the troops had long respected his stratagems, and now they wished to install him as leader.

sentences.zh: 洄自以老且病，推克融統軍務焉。

translations.literal: Hui, considering himself old and infirm, yielded military affairs to Kerong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, considering himself old and infirm, yielded command of military affairs to Kerong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋加檢校左散騎常侍，授以符節。

translations.literal: The court soon appointed him Acting Left Regular Attendant and conferred credentials of office.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed him Acting Left Regular Attendant and conferred the seals of command.

sentences.zh: ，遣使送方鎮及三軍時服，克融怒所賜疏弱，執中使以聞。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent bearing seasonal gifts for the frontier command and the three armies; Kerong, angered that what was granted was meager, seized the imperial messenger and reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys bearing seasonal gifts for the frontier command and the three armies; Kerong, angered that the gifts were meager, seized the imperial envoy and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上特優容，別命中使宣諭，仍改賜衣物，流其使楊文端等。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed him special forbearance, specially ordering a eunuch to announce this edict, and had different garments sent while banishing the envoy Yang Wenduan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor showed him special forbearance, ordered a separate envoy to announce the edict, sent different garments, and banished his envoy Yang Wenduan and others.

sentences.zh: 先是，克融執中使，奏稱：「竊聞陛下欲幸東都，請將兵馬並丁匠五千人，修理宮闕，迎候車駕。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kerong had seized the imperial messenger, he had memorialized: "I have heard that Your Majesty intends to visit the Eastern Capital. I request to lead troops and five thousand craftsmen to repair the palaces and await the imperial progress."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Kerong had seized the imperial envoy, he had memorialized: "I have heard that Your Majesty intends to visit the Eastern Capital. I ask leave to lead troops and five thousand craftsmen to repair the palaces and await the imperial progress."

sentences.zh: 」又上言無衣，擬於朝廷請三十萬端疋，以備一歲所費，不然則三軍不安。

translations.literal: He also petitioned that the armies had no clothing, proposing to request from the court three hundred thousand bolts of cloth for a year's expenses — otherwise the three armies would be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned that the armies lacked clothing and proposed to request three hundred thousand bolts from the court for a year's supply — otherwise the three armies would be unsettled.

sentences.zh: 天子怒其悖慢，取宰臣裴度謀，優容之，語見別卷。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was angered by his insolence and took counsel with the Chief Minister Pei Du, who indulged him — the full account is in another fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angered by his insolence and consulted Chief Minister Pei Du, who counselled indulgence; the full account appears in another fascicle.

sentences.zh: 克融官至檢校司空、吳興郡王。

translations.literal: Kerong eventually rose to Acting Minister of Works and Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong eventually rose to Acting Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，本州軍亂，殺之，子延齡亦遇害。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year the local army mutinied and killed him; his son Yanling also perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year the local army mutinied and killed him; his son Yanling was also killed.

sentences.zh: 次子延嗣竊立，尋為大將李載義所殺。

translations.literal: The second son Yansi seized power but was soon killed by the great general Li Zaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Yansi usurped command but was soon killed by the great general Li Zaiyi.

sentences.zh: 李載義李載義，字方谷，常山湣王之後。

translations.literal: Li Zaiyi — Li Zaiyi, courtesy name Fanggu, was a descendant of the Prince Min of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi, courtesy name Fanggu, was a descendant of Prince Min of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 代以武力稱，繼為幽州屬郡守。

translations.literal: His clan had risen through military prowess and he in turn became a prefectural governor in Youzhou's sphere.
translations.idiomatic: His family had risen through military prowess, and he in turn became a prefect in Youzhou's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 載義少孤，與鄉曲之不令者遊。

translations.literal: Zaiyi was orphaned young and kept company with unruly men of his district.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi was orphaned in youth and kept company with unruly men of his district.

sentences.zh: 有勇力，善挽強角牴。

translations.literal: He had courage and strength and excelled at drawing the bow and wrestling.
translations.idiomatic: He was brave and strong and excelled at drawing the heavy bow and at wrestling.

sentences.zh: 劉濟為幽州節度使，見而偉之，致於親軍，從征伐。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji became Military Governor of Youzhou, he was impressed by him and enrolled him in his personal guard, taking him on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji became Military Governor of Youzhou, he was impressed by him, enrolled him in his personal guard, and took him on campaigns.

sentences.zh: 以功遷衙前都知兵馬使，檢校光祿大夫、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Through merit he was promoted to Commander of the Vanguard Troops Who Know Military Affairs, with the titular posts of Acting Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to commander of the vanguard troops, with the titular posts of Acting Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Concurrent Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，幽師殺硃克融。

translations.literal: During the Baoli reign the Youzhou troops killed Zhu Kerong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli reign the Youzhou troops killed Zhu Kerong.

sentences.zh: 其子延嗣竊襲父位，不遵朝旨，虐用其人；

translations.literal: His son Yansi usurped his father's position, defied court directives, and cruelly mistreated the men under him;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yansi usurped his father's position, defied court directives, and cruelly mistreated his men;

sentences.zh: 載義遂殺之，數其罪以聞。

translations.literal: Zaiyi then killed him, enumerating his crimes in a report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi then killed him and reported his crimes to the throne in detail.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嘉之，拜檢校戶部尚書、兼御史大夫，封武威郡王，充幽州盧龍等軍節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong commended him, appointing him Acting Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffing him as Prince of Wuwei, and making him Deputy Military Commissioner of the Youzhou-Lulong armies with authority over frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong commended him, appointing him Acting Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffing him as Prince of Wuwei, and making him deputy military commissioner of the Youzhou-Lulong armies with authority over frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李同捷據滄景以邀襲父爵。

translations.literal: Before long Li Tongjie held Cangzhou and Jingzhou to claim his father's fief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Tongjie seized Cangzhou and Jingzhou to claim his father's fief.

sentences.zh: 載義上表，請討同捷以自效。

translations.literal: Zaiyi submitted a memorial asking to campaign against Tongjie to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi submitted a memorial asking to campaign against Tongjie to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其誠懇，特加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his sincerity and specially added the Acting Vice Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his sincerity and specially appointed him Acting Vice Director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 累破賊軍，以功加司空，進階金紫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the rebel armies; for his merit he was made Minister of Works and advanced to the Golden Purple grade.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated the rebel armies; for his merit he was made Minister of Works and advanced to the Golden Purple grade.

sentences.zh: ，平滄景，策勛加平章事，仍賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: When Cangzhou and Jingzhou were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Grand Counsellor for his merit and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangzhou and Jingzhou were pacified, he was made Grand Counsellor for his merit and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 四年，契丹寇邊，以兵擊走之，仍虜其名王，就加太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Khitans raided the border; he drove them off with troops and captured one of their princes, and was thereupon made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Khitans raided the border; he drove them off and captured one of their princes, and was thereupon made Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 五年春，為其部下楊志誠所逐，因入覲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he was driven out by his subordinate Yang Zhicheng and entered court to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was driven out by his subordinate Yang Zhicheng and came to court to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 上以載義有平滄景之功，又能恭順朝旨，再拜太保、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Zaiyi had merit in pacifying Cang-Jing and could respectfully follow court directives, again appointed him Grand Mentor and Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zaiyi had merit in pacifying Cang-Jing and could respectfully follow court directives, the Emperor again appointed him Grand Mentor and Grand Counsellor.

sentences.zh: 其年，改山南西道節度、觀察等使，兼興元尹。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Military Commissioner and Grand Coordinator of the Shanxi West Circuit, concurrently Governor of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to military commissioner and grand coordinator of the Shanxi West Circuit, concurrently governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷北都留守，兼太原尹，充河東節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to Northern Capital Protector, concurrently Governor of Taiyuan and Commissioner for the Hedong Military, Observation, and Administration Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was moved to Northern Capital Protector, concurrently governor of Taiyuan and commissioner for the Hedong military, observation, and administration circuits.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon after he was given the insignia of Grand Master Opening the Office with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was given the insignia of Grand Master Opening the Office with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復驃騎大將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning period began he was recalled from mourning to Grand General of Valiant Cavalry; his other posts remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's mourning began he was recalled from mourning as Grand General of Valiant Cavalry; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 回鶻每遣使入朝，所至強暴。

translations.literal: Whenever the Uyghurs sent envoys to court they were violent wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Uyghurs sent envoys to court, they were violent wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 邊城長吏多務茍安，不敢制之以法。

translations.literal: The senior officials of frontier cities mostly sought a quiet life and did not dare restrain them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials of frontier cities mostly sought a quiet life and did not dare restrain them by law.

sentences.zh: 但嚴兵防守，虜益驕悍，或突入市肆，暴橫無所憚。

translations.literal: They only mounted strict military guard, and the barbarians grew ever more arrogant — sometimes bursting into market streets and rampaging without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: They only mounted strict military guard, and the barbarians grew ever more arrogant — sometimes bursting into market streets and rampaging without restraint.

sentences.zh: 至是，有回鶻將軍李暢者，曉習中國事，知不能以法制馭，益驕恣。

translations.literal: On this occasion there was a Uyghur general named Li Chang who understood Chinese affairs and knew the court could not control them by law; he grew still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion there was a Uyghur general named Li Chang who understood Chinese affairs and knew the court could not control them by law; he grew still more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 鞭捶驛吏，貪求無已。

translations.literal: He flogged relay-station clerks and demanded gifts without end.
translations.idiomatic: He flogged relay-station clerks and demanded gifts without end.

sentences.zh: 載義因召李暢與語曰：「可汗使將軍朝貢，以固舅甥之好，不當使將軍暴踐中華。

translations.literal: Zaiyi therefore summoned Li Chang and said to him: "The Qaghan sent you, General, to pay tribute and strengthen the bond of uncle and nephew — you ought not to let the General trample over the Central Domain."
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi therefore summoned Li Chang and said to him: "The qaghan sent you, General, to pay tribute and strengthen the bond of uncle and nephew — you ought not to let the General trample over the Central Domain."

sentences.zh: 今朝廷饔餼至厚，所以禮蕃客也。

translations.literal: Now the court's generous provisions for you are very full — this is how foreign guests are treated.
translations.idiomatic: The court's provisions for you are very generous — this is how foreign guests are treated.

sentences.zh: 茍有不至，吏當坐死。

translations.literal: If anything falls short, the clerks would face execution.
translations.idiomatic: If anything falls short, the clerks would face execution.

sentences.zh: 若將軍之部伍不戢，淩侮上國，剽掠廬舍，載義必殺為盜者。

translations.literal: If the men under the General's command are undisciplined, insult the empire, and plunder dwellings, Zaiyi will surely kill anyone who acts as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: If the men under the General's command are undisciplined, insult the empire, and plunder dwellings, Zaiyi will surely kill anyone who acts as a bandit.

sentences.zh: 將軍勿以法令可輕而不戒勵之！

translations.literal: General, do not think the laws light and fail to warn and restrain your men!
translations.idiomatic: General, do not think the laws light and fail to warn and restrain your men!

sentences.zh: 」遂罷防守之兵，而使兩卒司其門。

translations.literal: He then dismissed the guard troops and had two soldiers watch his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed the guard troops and had two soldiers watch his gate.

sentences.zh: 虜知其心為下，無敢犯令。

translations.literal: The barbarians knew his resolve was firm and did not dare violate his orders.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians knew his resolve was firm and did not dare violate his orders.

sentences.zh: 九年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty and was posthumously honoured as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age fifty and was posthumously honoured as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 載義晚年驕恣，慘暴一方。

translations.literal: In his later years Zaiyi grew arrogant and cruelly terrorized the region.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Zaiyi grew arrogant and cruelly terrorized the region.

sentences.zh: 以楊志誠復為部下所逐，過太原，載義躬身毆擊，遂欲殺之，賴從事救解以免。

translations.literal: When Yang Zhicheng was in turn driven out by his subordinates and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi personally beat him and nearly killed him — only the intervention of a staff member saved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhicheng was in turn driven out by his subordinates and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi personally beat him and nearly killed him — only a staff member's intervention saved him.

sentences.zh: 然而擅殺志誠之妻孥及將卒。

translations.literal: Yet he killed Zhicheng's wife, children, and officers on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he killed Zhicheng's wife, children, and officers on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄其功，屈法不問。

translations.literal: The court credited his earlier merit and bent the law without prosecuting him.
translations.idiomatic: The court credited his earlier merit and bent the law without prosecuting him.

sentences.zh: 楊志誠楊志誠，為幽州後院副兵馬使，事李載義。

translations.literal: Yang Zhicheng — Yang Zhicheng was deputy commander of the rear-guard troops in Youzhou and served Li Zaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhicheng was deputy commander of the rear-guard troops in Youzhou and served Li Zaiyi.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷賜載義德政碑文。

translations.literal: At that time the court had granted Zaiyi a stele commemorating his virtuous governance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had granted Zaiyi a stele commemorating his virtuous governance.

sentences.zh: 載義延中使擊鞠，志誠亦與焉，遂於鞠場叫呼謀亂。

translations.literal: Zaiyi entertained the imperial envoy at cuju; Zhicheng was also present and suddenly shouted at the playing field plotting mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi entertained the imperial envoy at cuju; Zhicheng was also present and suddenly shouted at the playing field, plotting mutiny.

sentences.zh: 載義奔於易州，志誠乃為本道馬步都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Zaiyi fled to Yizhou; Zhicheng then became commander of infantry and cavalry for the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi fled to Yizhou; Zhicheng then became commander of infantry and cavalry for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 文宗聞之驚，急召宰臣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong heard of this he was alarmed and urgently summoned the Chief Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong heard of this he was alarmed and urgently summoned the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 時牛僧孺先至，上謂曰：「幽州今日之事可奈何？

translations.literal: Niu Sengru arrived first; the Emperor said to him: "What is to be done about today's events in Youzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru arrived first; the Emperor said to him: "What is to be done about today's events in Youzhou?"

sentences.zh: 」僧孺曰：「此不足煩聖慮，臣被召疾趨氣促，容臣稍緩息以對。

translations.literal: Sengru said: "This is not worth troubling Your Sacred Majesty. I was summoned in haste and am out of breath — allow me a moment to recover before answering."
translations.idiomatic: Sengru said: "This is not worth troubling Your Sacred Majesty. I was summoned in haste and am out of breath — allow me a moment to recover before answering."

sentences.zh: 」上良久曰：「卿以為不足憂，何也？

translations.literal: After a long pause the Emperor said: "You say it is not worth worry — why?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the Emperor said: "You say it is not worth worry — why?"

sentences.zh: 」僧孺對曰：「陛下以范陽得失系國家休戚耶？

translations.literal: Sengru replied: "Does Your Majesty believe the gain or loss of Fanyang affects the nation's weal and woe?"
translations.idiomatic: Sengru replied: "Does Your Majesty believe the gain or loss of Fanyang affects the nation's weal and woe?"

sentences.zh: 且自安、史之後，范陽非國家所有。

translations.literal: Since the An-Shi Rebellion, Fanyang has not truly belonged to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Since the An-Shi Rebellion, Fanyang has not truly belonged to the state.

sentences.zh: 前時劉總向化，以土地歸闕，朝廷約用錢八十萬貫，而未嘗得范陽尺布鬥粟上供天府；

translations.literal: When Liu Zong earlier submitted to the court and returned his territory, the court pledged eight hundred thousand strings of cash yet never received a single foot of Fanyang cloth or a dipper of grain for the imperial treasury;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong earlier submitted to the court and returned his territory, the court pledged eight hundred thousand strings of cash yet never received a single foot of Fanyang cloth or a dipper of grain for the imperial treasury;

sentences.zh: 則今日志誠之得，猶前日載義之得也。

translations.literal: then Zhicheng's gain today is the same as Zaiyi's gain was before.
translations.idiomatic: then Zhicheng's gain today is the same as Zaiyi's gain was before.

sentences.zh: 陛下但因而撫之，亦事之宜也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only accept this and soothe him — that is also what the situation calls for.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need only accept this and soothe him — that is also what the situation calls for.

sentences.zh: 且范陽，國家所賴者，以其北捍突厥，不令南寇。

translations.literal: Moreover Fanyang is what the state relies upon because it shields the north against the Turks and keeps them from raiding south.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Fanyang is what the state relies upon because it shields the north against the Turks and keeps them from raiding south.

sentences.zh: 今若假志誠節鉞，惜其土地，必自為力。

translations.literal: Now if you grant Zhicheng the seals of command but withhold his territory, he will surely fight on his own behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Now if you grant Zhicheng the seals of command but withhold his territory, he will surely fight on his own behalf.

sentences.zh: 則爪牙之用，固不計於逆順。

translations.literal: Then his claws and teeth will be used regardless of loyalty or rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Then his claws and teeth will be used regardless of loyalty or rebellion.

sentences.zh: 臣固曰不足煩聖慮。

translations.literal: I repeat that it is not worth troubling Your Sacred Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I repeat that it is not worth troubling Your Sacred Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上大喜曰：「如卿之言，吾洗然矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "As you say, my mind is cleared."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "As you say, my mind is cleared."

sentences.zh: 」尋以嘉王運遙領節度，以志誠為節度觀察留後，檢校左散騎常侍，兼幽州左司馬。

translations.literal: Soon the Prince of Jia, Li Yun, was made titular Military Commissioner while Zhicheng was made Acting Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner, Acting Left Regular Attendant, and Concurrent Left Marshal of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Jia, Li Yun, was made titular military commissioner while Zhicheng was made acting military commissioner and observation commissioner, Acting Left Regular Attendant, and concurrent Left Marshal of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋改檢校工部尚書、節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Acting Minister of Works, Deputy Military Commissioner, with authority over frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Acting Minister of Works, deputy military commissioner, with authority over frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詔下，進奏官徐迪詣中書白宰相曰：「軍中不識朝廷體位，只知自尚書改僕射為遷，何知工部轉吏部為美？

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the memorial envoy Xu Di went to the Secretariat and told the Chief Ministers: "The army does not understand the court's hierarchy of offices — they only know that a change from Vice Director to Director is a promotion; how would they know that transfer from Works to Personnel is an honour?"
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the memorial envoy Xu Di went to the Secretariat and told the chief ministers: "The army does not understand the court's hierarchy of offices — they only know that a change from Vice Director to Director is a promotion; how would they know that transfer from Works to Personnel is an honour?"

sentences.zh: 且軍士盛飾以待新恩，一旦復為尚書，軍中必慚。

translations.literal: The troops have prepared splendid dress awaiting the new favour; if they suddenly become Vice Director again the army will be shamed.
translations.idiomatic: The troops have prepared splendid dress awaiting the new favour; if they suddenly become Vice Director again the army will be shamed.

sentences.zh: 今中使往彼，其勢恐不得出。

translations.literal: Now if an imperial envoy goes there, I fear he will not be allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Now if an imperial envoy goes there, I fear he will not be allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 」及使至，其傔奔還，奏曰：「楊志誠怒不得僕射，三軍亦有怨言。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived his attendants fled back and reported: "Yang Zhicheng is angry at not receiving the Directorship; the three armies also have complaints."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived his attendants fled back and reported: "Yang Zhicheng is angry at not receiving the directorship; the three armies also have complaints."

sentences.zh: 春衣使魏寶義、兼他使焦奉鸞，尹士恭，並為志誠縶留矣。

translations.literal: The spring-clothing envoy Wei Baoyi, together with other envoys Jiao Fengluan and Yin Shigong, have all been detained by Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The spring-clothing envoy Wei Baoyi, together with other envoys Jiao Fengluan and Yin Shigong, have all been detained by Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 」志誠遣將王文穎謝恩，並讓官，復賜官告批答，文穎不受而歸。

translations.literal: Zhicheng sent his general Wang Wenying to thank the throne and decline the appointment; the court again sent patent letters of appointment with replies, but Wenying would not accept them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng sent his general Wang Wenying to thank the throne and decline the appointment; the court again sent patent letters of appointment with replies, but Wenying would not accept them and returned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷納裴度言，務以含垢，下詔諭之，因再遣使加尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: The court adopted Pei Du's advice to swallow the affront, issued an edict reassuring him, and sent envoys again to appoint him Acting Vice Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Pei Du's advice to swallow the affront, issued an edict reassuring him, and sent envoys again to appoint him Acting Vice Director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 八年，為三軍所逐，則立史元忠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was driven out by the three armies and Shi Yuanzhong was installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was driven out by the three armies and Shi Yuanzhong was installed.

sentences.zh: 元忠進志誠所造袞龍衣二副及被服鞍韉，皆繡飾鸞鳳日月之形，或為王字。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong presented two sets of dragon robes and saddle trappings that Zhicheng had made, all embroidered with phoenixes, sun and moon, or the character for "king."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong presented two sets of dragon robes and saddle trappings that Zhicheng had made, all embroidered with phoenixes, sun and moon, or the character for "king."

sentences.zh: 因付御史臺按問，流嶺南。

translations.literal: He handed them to the Censorate for investigation and Zhicheng was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He handed them to the Censorate for investigation and Zhicheng was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 行至商州，殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached Shangzhou he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shangzhou he was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，元忠既逐志誠，詔以通王淳遙領節度，授元忠左散騎常侍、幽州大都督府左司馬、知府事，充節度留後。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhong had first driven out Zhicheng, the edict made Prince of Tong Li Chun titular Military Commissioner and appointed Yuanzhong Left Regular Attendant, Left Marshal of the Youzhou Grand Protectorate with authority over prefectural affairs, and Acting Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhong had first driven out Zhicheng, the edict made Prince of Tong Li Chun titular military commissioner and appointed Yuanzhong Left Regular Attendant, Left Marshal of the Youzhou Grand Protectorate with authority over prefectural affairs, and acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉檢校工部尚書、節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, Deputy Military Commissioner, with authority over frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, deputy military commissioner, with authority over frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 後為偏將陳行泰所殺。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by the junior general Chen Xingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was killed by the junior general Chen Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 張仲武張仲武，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu — Zhang Zhongwu was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 仲武少業《左氏春秋》，擲筆為薊北雄武軍使。

translations.literal: In youth Zhongwu studied the Zuozhuan, then cast aside his brush and became commander of the Xiongwei army in northern Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhongwu studied the Zuozhuan, then cast aside his brush and became commander of the Xiongwei army in northern Ji.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，陳行泰殺節度使史元忠，權主留後。

translations.literal: In the early Huichang era Chen Xingtai killed Military Governor Shi Yuanzhong and held power as Acting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huichang era Chen Xingtai killed Military Governor Shi Yuanzhong and held power as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄而，行泰又為次將張絳所殺，令三軍上表，請降符節。

translations.literal: Before long Xingtai was in turn killed by the next-ranking general Zhang Jiang, who had the three armies submit a memorial requesting the grant of credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xingtai was in turn killed by the next-ranking general Zhang Jiang, who had the three armies submit a memorial requesting the grant of credentials.

sentences.zh: 時仲武遣軍吏吳仲舒表請以本軍伐叛。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongwu sent the army clerk Wu Zhongshu to memorialize asking that this army be used to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhongwu sent the army clerk Wu Zhongshu to memorialize asking that this army be used to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 上遣宰臣詢其事，仲舒曰：「絳與行泰，皆是遊客，主軍人心不附。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Chief Ministers to inquire; Zhongshu said: "Jiang and Xingtai are both outsiders — the men leading the army do not trust them."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent chief ministers to inquire; Zhongshu said: "Jiang and Xingtai are both outsiders — the men leading the army do not trust them."

sentences.zh: 仲武是軍中舊將張光朝之子，年五十餘，兼曉儒書，老於戎事，性抱忠義，願歸心闕廷。

translations.literal: Zhongwu is an old officer of the army, son of Zhang Guangchao, over fifty years old, versed in Confucian learning, long experienced in military affairs, and by nature loyal and righteous — he wishes to submit his heart to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu is an old officer of the army, son of Zhang Guangchao, over fifty years old, versed in Confucian learning, long experienced in military affairs, and by nature loyal and righteous — he wishes to submit his heart to the court."

sentences.zh: 」李德裕因奏：「陳行泰、張絳皆令大將上奏，邀求節旄，所以必不可與。

translations.literal: Li Deyu thereupon memorialized: "Both Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang have had their great generals submit memorials demanding the insignia of command — therefore they must absolutely not be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu thereupon memorialized: "Both Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang have had their great generals submit memorials demanding the insignia of command — therefore they must absolutely not be granted."

sentences.zh: 今仲武上表布誠，先陳密款，因而拔用，即似有名。

translations.literal: Now Zhongwu submitted a memorial declaring his sincerity, first setting forth secret pledges of loyalty; he was then promoted and appointed, which seemed to lend the move justification.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu now memorialized the throne with professions of loyalty, laying out secret pledges first—and on that basis was elevated to office, as though the appointment had always been meant for him.

sentences.zh: 」許之，乃授兵馬留後，詔撫王纮遙領節度。

translations.literal: The request was granted, and he was appointed acting commander of troops; an edict made Wang Hong of Zhaofu titular military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted. Zhongwu was made acting military commissioner, while Wang Hong of Zhaofu was ordered to hold the governorship in name from a distance.

sentences.zh: 尋改仲武節度副大使、知節度事，檢校工部尚書、幽州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫、蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongwu was changed to Deputy Military Governor and Acting Governor, Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of the Youzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, also Censor-in-Chief, and Prince of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made deputy military governor with full charge of the circuit, acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Youzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 俄而回鶻擾邊。

translations.literal: Before long the Uyghurs disturbed the border.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Uyghurs began raiding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時回鶻有將勒那頡啜擁赤心宰相一族七千帳，東逼漁陽。

translations.literal: At that time among the Uyghurs there was a general, Le Nazhichuo, who led the Chixin Chancellor's clan of seven thousand tents, pressing east toward Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: A Uyghur general named Le Nazhichuo had gathered seven thousand tents of the Chixin Chancellor's clan and was driving east against Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 仲武遣其弟仲至與裨將遊奉寰、王如清等，率銳兵三萬人大破之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu sent his brother Zhongzhi, together with subordinate generals You Fenghuan, Wang Ruqing, and others, to lead thirty thousand crack troops and inflict a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu dispatched his brother Zhongzhi with the subordinate generals You Fenghuan and Wang Ruqing to take thirty thousand elite troops and break them utterly.

sentences.zh: 前後收其侯王貴族千餘人，降三萬人，獲牛馬、橐駝、旗纛、罽幕不可勝計。

translations.literal: Before and after, they captured more than a thousand of their princes, kings, and nobles, accepted the surrender of thirty thousand men, and seized cattle, horses, camels, banners, standards, and felt tents beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting they took more than a thousand Uyghur princes and nobles, accepted the surrender of thirty thousand men, and captured cattle, horses, camels, banners, standards, and felt tents beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 遣從事李周瞳、牙門將國從，相次獻捷。

translations.literal: He dispatched the staff officer Li Zhoutong and the gate officer Guo Cong in succession to report victories.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his aide Li Zhoutong and gate officer Guo Cong, one after another, to the capital with news of victory.

sentences.zh: 詔加檢校兵部尚書，兼東面招撫回鶻使。

translations.literal: An edict additionally appointed him Acting Minister of War and concurrently Commissioner for Pacifying the Uyghurs on the Eastern Front.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then promoted him to acting Minister of War and made him commissioner for winning over the Uyghurs on the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 先是，奚、契丹皆有回鶻監護使，督以歲貢，且為漢諜。

translations.literal: Previously, both the Xi and the Khitan had Uyghur supervisory envoys who supervised their annual tribute and also served as spies for the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Xi and Khitan had each been assigned Uyghur overseers to collect annual tribute and report back as Tang spies.

sentences.zh: 至是，遣裨將石公緒等諭意兩部，凡戮八百餘人。

translations.literal: At this time he dispatched the subordinate generals Shi Gongxu and others to convey his intentions to both tribes; in all more than eight hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu now sent subordinates such as Shi Gongxu to make his will known to both peoples, and in all more than eight hundred were put to death.

sentences.zh: 又回鶻初遣宣門將軍等四十七人，詭詞結歡，潛伺邊隙。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Uyghurs had at first sent forty-seven men, including Gate Guards, to forge friendly relations with deceitful words while secretly watching for openings on the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had also first sent forty-seven envoys, among them gate guards, speaking fair words to win favor while secretly probing the frontier for weakness.

sentences.zh: 仲武使密賂其下，盡得陰謀。

translations.literal: Zhongwu had their subordinates secretly bribed and fully learned the secret plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu secretly bribed men in their party and learned the whole of their hidden design.

sentences.zh: 且欲馳入五原，驅掠雜虜。

translations.literal: They also intended to gallop into Wuyuan and drive off plunder from various barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They planned besides to ride hard into Wuyuan and sweep the mixed frontier peoples before them.

sentences.zh: 遂逗遛其使，緩彼師期。

translations.literal: He then detained their envoys and delayed their military timetable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu therefore kept their envoys in hand and put off the date they had set to march.

sentences.zh: 人馬病死，竟不遣之。

translations.literal: Men and horses died of sickness, and in the end they were not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Their men and horses sickened and died, and in the end the envoys were never released.

sentences.zh: 回鶻烏介可汗既敗，不敢近邊，乃依康居求活，盡徙餘種，寄托黑車子部。

translations.literal: After the Uyghur Khan Wujie was defeated, he dared not approach the border; he then sought survival by relying on Kangju, moved all the remaining tribesmen, and entrusted themselves to the Black Cart tribe.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghur khan Wujie had been broken, he no longer dared come near the border. He turned toward Kangju to save himself, moved every remnant of his people, and took shelter with the Black Cart tribe.

sentences.zh: 仲武由是威加北狄，表請於薊北立《紀聖功銘》，敕李德裕為之文，其銘曰：

translations.literal: Zhongwu thereby extended his authority over the northern barbarians. He submitted a memorial requesting that a "Record of Sagely Achievements" inscription be erected north of Ji; the emperor ordered Li Deyu to compose the text. The inscription reads:
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu's prestige over the northern tribes was now complete. He memorialized asking that a Record of Sagely Achievements inscription be set up north of Ji, and the throne commanded Li Deyu to write it. The inscription says:

sentences.zh: 仲武歷官至司徒、中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Zhongwu successively reached the posts of Minister of Education and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the course of his career Zhongwu rose to Minister of Education and Grand Councellor.

sentences.zh: 大中年卒，謚曰莊。

translations.literal: He died in the Dazhong era; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dazhong reign and was posthumously titled Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子 直方子直方，以幽州節度副使襲父位。

translations.literal: His son Zhifang succeeded to his father's position as Deputy Military Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhifang inherited the post, serving as deputy military governor of Youzhou in his father's stead.

sentences.zh: 動多不法，慮為將卒所圖。

translations.literal: His actions were often unlawful, and he feared being plotted against by the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He behaved lawlessly in many matters and grew afraid the troops might turn on him.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，托以遊獵，奔赴闕庭，尋授金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, winter, he claimed to go hunting, hurried to the imperial court, and was soon appointed General of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, during winter, he pleaded a hunting trip, fled to the capital, and was soon made a general of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 直方性率暴，行豪奪之事，以罪累貶柳州司馬。

translations.literal: Zhifang was by nature reckless and violent; he committed acts of forcible seizure, and for accumulated crimes was demoted to Military Advisor of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang was rough and overbearing by nature and lived by seizure and force; repeated offenses eventually got him demoted to military advisor at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷右驍衛將軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to General of the Right Xiaowei Guard, serving in the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was moved to general of the Right Xiaowei Guard with duty at the Eastern Capital branch court.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，位至羽林統軍。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era he reached the post of Commander of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiantong he rose to command the Forest of Feathers guard.

sentences.zh: 中和歲，賊巢犯闕，公卿恃其豪，多隱藏於第。

translations.literal: In the Zhonghe years, when the rebel Huang Chao attacked the capital, court officials trusted in his martial prowess, and many concealed themselves in his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhonghe years, when Huang Chao's rebels stormed the capital, high officials put their faith in Zhifang's fighting name and many took refuge in his house.

sentences.zh: 直方納招亡命，謀欲劫巢。

translations.literal: Zhifang recruited and harbored fugitives, plotting to raid Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang gathered runaways and outlaws and plotted a strike against Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 或有告者，由是以兵圍而害之。

translations.literal: Someone reported this, whereupon troops surrounded him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When word of it got out, armed men surrounded him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 張允伸張允伸，字逢昌，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunshen — Zhang Yunshen, styled Fengchang, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunshen, courtesy name Fengchang, came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秀，檀州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu was Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiu had been prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖巖，納降軍使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Commissioner of the Surrendered Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had served as commissioner of the surrendered army.

sentences.zh: 父朝掖，贈太尉。

translations.literal: His father Chaoye was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chaoye was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 允申世仕幽州軍門，累職至押衙，兼馬步都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunshen for generations served in the Youzhou military command, rising through successive posts to Chief of Staff and concurrently Commissioner of both Cavalry and Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang family had long served in the Youzhou armies; Yunshen himself worked his way up to chief of staff and commander of all horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 大中四年，戎帥周綝寢疾，表允伸為留後，朝廷可其奏，加右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong, the military governor Zhou Can fell gravely ill and recommended Yunshen as acting military governor; the court approved his memorial and promoted Yunshen to Right Regular Mounted Escort.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 4 the frontier commander Zhou Can fell seriously ill and recommended Yunshen as acting governor. The court assented and made Yunshen Right Regular Mounted Escort.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，詔賜旌節，遷檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter an edict granted him the banner and credentials of command, and he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the throne bestowed the banner and commission of full authority and promoted him to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: ，累加至光祿大夫、檢校司徒、兼太傅、同中書門下平章事、燕國公。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Education, concurrently Grand Tutor, Grand Councillor, and Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Further honors followed in turn: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Education, Grand Tutor, Grand Councillor, and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十年，徐人作亂，請以弟允臯領兵伐叛，懿宗不允。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the people of Xu rebelled; he requested that his brother Yungang lead troops to suppress the rebellion, but Emperor Yizong did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Xu rose in revolt, he asked leave to send his brother Yungang against the rebels; Emperor Yizong refused.

sentences.zh: 進助軍米五十萬石，鹽二萬石。

translations.literal: He submitted fifty thousand shi of grain and twenty thousand shi of salt as military aid.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sent fifty thousand shi of grain and twenty thousand shi of salt to support the campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之，賜以錦彩、玉帶、金銀器等。

translations.literal: An edict praised this and bestowed upon him brocades, a jade belt, gold and silver vessels, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised the gift and rewarded him with brocades, a jade belt, gold and silver ware, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 冬，又加特進，兼侍中。

translations.literal: In winter he was further granted the rank of Special Advancement and concurrently appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was given the rank of Special Advancement and made Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以風恙拜章請就醫藥，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, citing wind-related illness, he submitted a memorial requesting leave for medical treatment; the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized, pleading illness brought on by wind, to seek medical leave; the throne allowed it.

sentences.zh: 以子簡會檢校工部尚書，充節度副大使。

translations.literal: His son Jianhui was appointed Acting Minister of Works and served as Deputy Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianhui was made acting Minister of Works and deputy military governor in his place.

sentences.zh: 十三年，允伸再上表進納所賜旌節。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Yunshen again submitted a memorial returning the banner and credentials of command that had been granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Yunshen memorialized again, offering back the banner and commission the throne had given him.

sentences.zh: 朝命未至，其年正月二十五日卒，年八十八。

translations.literal: Before the court's response arrived, on the twenty-fifth day of the first month of that year he died, aged eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The court's reply had not yet come when, on the twenty-fifth day of the first month that year, he died at eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 再贈太尉，謚曰忠烈。

translations.literal: He was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor; his posthumous title was Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was again honored after death as Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous name Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 允伸領鎮凡二十三年，克勤克儉，比歲豐登。

translations.literal: Yunshen held the garrison for twenty-three years in all, diligent and frugal; year after year the harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Yunshen governed the frontier twenty-three years in all, tireless and sparing; harvest after harvest ran rich.

sentences.zh: 邊鄙無虞，軍民用乂。

translations.literal: The border regions were free from alarm; soldiers and civilians lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The marches knew no trouble, and soldiers and people alike lived at ease.

sentences.zh: 至今談者美之。

translations.literal: Even to this day those who speak of it praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Men still speak of him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 有子十四人。

translations.literal: He had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 簡真，幽府左司馬，先允伸卒。

translations.literal: Jian Zhen was Left Assistant Administrator of the Youzhou prefectural staff; he predeceased Yunshen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Zhen served as Left Assistant Administrator on the Youzhou prefectural staff and died before Zhang Yunshen.

sentences.zh: 簡壽，右領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Jian Shou was Grand General of the Right Victorious Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shou held the post of Grand General of the Right Victorious Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 餘或升朝籍，或為刺史、郡佐。

translations.literal: The rest either entered the court registry or served as prefects and county aides.
translations.idiomatic: The others either rose into court ranks or served as prefects and county administrators.

sentences.zh: 張公素張公素，范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongsu — Zhang Gongsu was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，為幽州軍校。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong period he was an officer in the Youzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era he served as an officer in the Youzhou army.

sentences.zh: 事張允伸，累遷至平州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Zhang Yunshen and was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Yunshen he rose through successive promotions to Prefect of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 允伸卒，子簡會權主留後事，公素領本郡兵赴焉。

translations.literal: When Yunshen died, his son Jian Hui provisionally took charge of the acting governor's affairs, and Gongsu led troops from his home command to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunshen's death, his son Jian Hui provisionally handled the military governor's affairs, and Gongsu marched there at the head of his home command's troops.

sentences.zh: 三軍素畏公素威望，簡會知力不能制，即時出奔，遂立為帥。

translations.literal: The three armies had long feared Gongsu's prestige; Jian Hui knew his strength could not control them, fled at once, and Gongsu was thereupon installed as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies had long stood in awe of Gongsu's authority; realizing he lacked the power to control them, Jian Hui fled on the spot, and the troops thereupon installed Gongsu as their commander.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋授旌節，累加至中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The court soon granted him banners and credentials, and he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon invested him with banners and credentials of command, and he was promoted in stages to Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 無幾，李茂勛奪其位，公素歸闕，貶復州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Before long Li Maoxun seized his position; Gongsu returned to court and was demoted to Recorder of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Li Maoxun displaced him; Gongsu returned to the capital and was demoted to Recorder of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李可舉李可舉，本回鶻阿布思之族也。

translations.literal: Li Keju — Li Keju was originally of the Uyghur Abusi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keju was originally a member of the Uyghur Abusi clan.

sentences.zh: 張仲武破回鶻，可舉父茂勛與本部侯王降焉。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhongwu defeated the Uyghurs, Keju's father Maoxun and the tribal princes of his division surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Zhongwu routed the Uyghurs, Keju's father Maoxun and the tribal chiefs of his band submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 茂勛善騎射，性沈毅，仲武器之。

translations.literal: Maoxun excelled at mounted archery and was deep and resolute by nature; Zhongwu valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun was skilled in horsemanship and archery and steady by temperament, and Zhongwu held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 常遣拓邊，以功封郡王，賜姓名。

translations.literal: He was often sent to expand the frontier; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Prince of a commandery and granted a surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly dispatched to expand the frontier, he was enfeoffed as Prince of a commandery for his achievements and given a formal Chinese name.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，納降軍使陳貢言者，幽之宿將，人所信服。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiantong, the Surrendered Troops Commissioner Chen Gongyan was a veteran general of Youzhou whom all trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xiantong reign, Chen Gongyan, Commissioner for Surrendered Troops, was a seasoned Youzhou general in whom the men placed their trust.

sentences.zh: 茂勛密謀劫而殺之，聲雲貢言舉兵。

translations.literal: Maoxun secretly plotted to seize and kill him, spreading word that Gongyan was raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun secretly plotted to seize and kill him, putting about the story that Gongyan had risen in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 張公素以兵逆擊不利，公素走，茂勛入城，軍民方知其非貢言也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongsu met him with troops but was defeated; Gongsu fled, and when Maoxun entered the city the army and people only then learned it had not been Gongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu marched out to oppose him but was beaten; Gongsu fled, and only when Maoxun entered the city did soldiers and civilians realize the revolt had not been Gongyan's doing.

sentences.zh: 既有其眾，遂推而立之，朝廷即降符節。

translations.literal: Now holding the troops, they thereupon pushed forward and installed him, and the court immediately bestowed credentials of office.
translations.idiomatic: Having secured the army, they thereupon raised him up as leader, and the court promptly granted him the seals of command.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以疾告老，授右僕射致仕，表可舉自節度副使、幽州左司馬加右散騎常侍，為節度留後。

translations.literal: Before long, citing illness he requested retirement; he was appointed Right Vice Director and retired, and memorialized that Keju be promoted from Deputy Military Governor and Left Assistant Administrator of Youzhou to Right Regular Attendant and made Acting Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, pleading illness he asked to retire; he was granted the title of Right Vice Director and allowed to leave office, and he memorialized that Keju be promoted from Deputy Military Governor and Left Assistant Administrator of Youzhou to Right Regular Attendant and appointed Acting Military Governor.

sentences.zh: 中和中，累官至檢校太尉。

translations.literal: During the Zhonghe era he rose through repeated promotions to Acting Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhonghe period he advanced through successive appointments to Acting Grand General.

sentences.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was at its height, he secretly formed an alliance with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhonghe reign, with Li Keyong of Taiyuan at the height of his military power, Keju entered into a secret alliance with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。

translations.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in Shandong and in the end become a threat to him, so he sent envoys to persuade Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from behind; then together with Zhenzhou he plotted to raise troops, adding that Yizhou and Dingzhou were remnants of Yan and Zhao — if Yun obtained the land they would rectify the borders and divide the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Keju feared that Keyong would eye Shandong and eventually become a menace to him, so he sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack from the rear; he then conspired with Zhenzhou to take up arms, arguing that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that once Yunzhong seized the territory they would set the boundaries aright and partition the land.

sentences.zh: 時可舉遣將李全忠攻易州。

translations.literal: At that time Keju dispatched General Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Keju sent General Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 有次將劉仁恭者，多權數；

translations.literal: There was a deputy commander named Liu Rengong, full of stratagems;
translations.idiomatic: Among them was a deputy commander named Liu Rengong, a man rich in wiles;

sentences.zh: 攻之彌月不下，乃穴地道以入。

translations.literal: after attacking for a full month without taking the city, they dug a tunnel to enter.
translations.idiomatic: when a month of assault failed to bring the city down, they tunneled beneath the walls to break in.

sentences.zh: 其城既下，易州士卒稍驕。

translations.literal: Once the city had fallen, the troops at Yizhou grew somewhat arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, the soldiers occupying Yizhou grew somewhat overconfident.

sentences.zh: 王處存引輕軍三千，以羊皮蒙之，夜伏於城外，仍別於間道以騎士伺之。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun led three thousand light troops, covered them with sheepskins, and lay in ambush outside the walls by night; meanwhile he posted cavalry along a side path to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun led three thousand light infantrymen, disguised them with sheepskins, and hid outside the walls by night, while also placing horsemen along a hidden route to keep watch.

sentences.zh: 燕軍望見，謂之群羊，爭趨焉。

translations.literal: The Yan army saw them and, taking them for a flock of sheep, rushed headlong toward them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops spotted them, mistook them for a herd of sheep, and charged eagerly toward them.

sentences.zh: 處存乘其無部伍，一擊大敗之，尋復其城。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun seized the moment when they were disordered, struck once and routed them utterly, and soon recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun struck while they were in disarray, crushing them in a single blow, and soon retook the city.

sentences.zh: 全忠遁歸，懼可舉罪之，收其餘眾，反攻幽州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong fled back, fearing Keju would punish him; he gathered his remaining troops and counterattacked Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong fled homeward, afraid Keju would hold him accountable; he rallied his surviving forces and turned back to assault Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 可舉危急，收集其族，登樓自燔而死。

translations.literal: Keju, in dire straits, gathered his clan, ascended a tower, and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Keju, brought to the brink of ruin, gathered his kinsmen, climbed a tower, and immolated himself.

sentences.zh: 李全忠李全忠，范陽人。

translations.literal: Li Quanzhong — Li Quanzhong was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanzhong was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 廣明中，為棣州司馬。

translations.literal: During the Guangming era he served as Assistant Administrator of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangming period he served as Assistant Administrator of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 有蘆生於室，一尺三節，心惡之。

translations.literal: Reeds grew in his room, a foot high with three joints; he was troubled at heart by this.
translations.idiomatic: Reeds sprouted in his bedchamber, standing a foot tall in three sections, and the sight filled him with unease.

sentences.zh: 謂別駕張建曰：「吾室生蘆，無乃怪歟？

translations.literal: He said to Vice-Prefect Zhang Jian, "Reeds have grown in my room — might this not be an omen?
translations.idiomatic: He said to Vice-Prefect Zhang Jian, "Reeds have sprung up in my room — could this be an ill omen?"

sentences.zh: 」建曰：「蘆，茅類，得澤而滋，公家有茅土之慶，殆天意乎！

translations.literal: Jian replied, "Reed is of the same kind as thatch; given moisture it thrives. Your household has the auspice of enfeoffment with thatch — could this be Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian replied, "Reed belongs to the rush family; where there is moisture it flourishes. In your house this is the sign of a fief sealed with thatch — surely it is Heaven's will!"

sentences.zh: 其生三節，必傳節鉞者三人。

translations.literal: That it sprouted three joints means three men in succession will hold the commander's seal and axe.
translations.idiomatic: That it bore three joints foretells that three generations will pass the seal and axe of command."

sentences.zh: 公勉樹功名，無忘斯言。

translations.literal: Sir, strive to build merit and fame, and do not forget these words.
translations.idiomatic: My lord, strive to win glory and achievement, and do not forget what I have said."

sentences.zh: 」全忠秩滿還鄉里，事節度使李可舉為牙將。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong's term expired he returned to his home district and served Military Governor Li Keju as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When his term of office ended, Quanzhong returned to his home district and entered the service of Military Governor Li Keju as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 時可舉兵鋒方盛，欲與鎮人分易、定，遣全忠將兵攻之，為定州軍大敗於易水。

translations.literal: At that time Keju's military power was at its height; wishing with the men of Zhenzhou to divide Yizhou and Dingzhou, he sent Quanzhong to lead troops against them, but the Dingzhou army routed him utterly at the Yishui River.
translations.idiomatic: Keju's armies were then at their peak; intending to carve up Yizhou and Dingzhou with the forces of Zhenzhou, he dispatched Quanzhong to attack them, but the Dingzhou army crushed him on the banks of the Yishui.

sentences.zh: 全忠懼，率其餘眾掩攻幽州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, in fear, led his remaining troops in a surprise attack on Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Quanzhong gathered his surviving troops and launched a surprise assault on Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 可舉死。

translations.literal: Keju died.
translations.idiomatic: Keju perished.

sentences.zh: 三軍推全忠為留後，朝廷因以節鉞授之，春也。

translations.literal: The three armies pushed Quanzhong forward as acting governor, and the court thereupon granted him the seal and axe — it was spring.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies proclaimed Quanzhong acting military governor, and the court thereupon invested him with the seal and axe of command; it was spring.

sentences.zh: 全忠卒，子匡威自襲父位，稱留後。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong died, his son Kuangwei seized his father's position on his own authority and styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanzhong's death, his son Kuangwei took his father's post by force and declared himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 匡威素稱豪爽，屬遇亂離，繕甲燕薊，有吞四海之志。

translations.literal: Kuangwei had long been known for bold magnanimity; amid the turmoil of the times he readied armor in Yan and Ji, harboring the ambition to swallow the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei had long been famed for open-handed boldness; caught in an age of upheaval, he drilled troops throughout Yan and Ji and nursed the ambition to rule all beneath Heaven.

sentences.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。

translations.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly pulled Kuangwei into wars with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou, and their armies fought in alliance for years on end.

sentences.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu era, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed Li Cunxiao, a general of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou lured away Li Cunxiao, a general of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。

translations.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to chastise him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Keyong mobilized additional forces to punish him.

sentences.zh: 時鎔童幼，求援於燕；

translations.literal: Wang Rong was then young, and sought aid from Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong was still a boy at the time, and he appealed to Yan for help;

sentences.zh: 匡威親率軍應之。

translations.literal: Kuangwei personally led an army in response.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei marched out in person to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing Pass; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass; Wang Rong again appealed for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

sentences.zh: 匡威弟匡籌，妻張氏有國色。

translations.literal: Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou had a wife, Lady Zhang, of national beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou had a wife, Lady Zhang, whose beauty was famed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 師將發，家人會別，匡威酒酣，留張氏報之。

translations.literal: When the army was about to depart, the family gathered to bid farewell; Kuangwei, deep in drink, detained Lady Zhang to keep his brother company.
translations.idiomatic: As the army was about to march, the family gathered to say farewell; Kuangwei, drunk, kept Lady Zhang behind to keep his brother company.

sentences.zh: 匡籌私懷忿怒，匡威軍至博野，匡籌乃據城自為節度。

translations.literal: Kuangchou secretly nursed anger; when Kuangwei's army reached Boye, Kuangchou seized the city and proclaimed himself military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou secretly seethed with rage; when Kuangwei's army reached Boye, Kuangchou seized the city and installed himself as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 匡威部下聞之，亡歸者半。

translations.literal: When Kuangwei's subordinates heard of this, half deserted and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuangwei's men heard the news, half of them deserted and went home.

sentences.zh: 匡威退無歸路，將入覲京師。

translations.literal: Kuangwei, retreating with no road home, was about to enter the capital to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei, retreating with nowhere to go, prepared to enter the capital and pay homage.

sentences.zh: 時匡威留於深州，遣判官李抱貞奉章以聞。

translations.literal: At that time Kuangwei remained at Shenzhou and sent his aide Li Baozhen to submit a memorial reporting this.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei was then staying at Shenzhou and sent his aide Li Baozhen to the capital with a memorial reporting his situation.

sentences.zh: 屬京師大亂之後，聞匡威來朝，市人震恐，咸曰「金頭王來謀社稷」，士庶有亡竄山谷者。

translations.literal: This came just after great turmoil in the capital; when word spread that Kuangwei was coming to court, townspeople were alarmed, all saying "The Gold-Headed King is coming to plot against the realm," and officials and commoners fled to hide in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: This came just after the capital had been thrown into chaos; when word spread that Kuangwei was coming to court, the townspeople panicked, crying that "the Gold-Headed King is coming to seize the throne," and many officials and commoners fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 匡威其實不行，欲圖鎮州，示無留意。

translations.literal: Kuangwei in fact did not go; he wished to seize Zhenzhou and showed no intent to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei never actually went; he meant to take Zhenzhou and gave no sign of leaving.

sentences.zh: 鎔以匡威再來援己，致其失師，遣使迎歸府第，父事之。

translations.literal: Rong, because Kuangwei had come twice to aid him and thereby lost his troops, sent envoys to welcome him back to the mansion and treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kuangwei had marched to his aid twice and thereby lost his army, Rong sent envoys to welcome him to his mansion and treated him like a father.

sentences.zh: 匡威為鎔城郛繕甲，指陳方略，視鎔如子。

translations.literal: Kuangwei repaired the walls and armor for Rong, outlined strategy, and regarded Rong as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei repaired Rong's walls and armor, laid out strategy for him, and looked on him as a son.

sentences.zh: 每陰謀驟施，以悅人心。

translations.literal: He constantly plotted and acted abruptly to win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly hatched schemes and acted suddenly to win hearts.

sentences.zh: 鎮之三軍，素忠於王氏，惡其所為。

translations.literal: The three armies of Zhen had long been loyal to the Wang clan and hated what he did.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies of Zhen had long been loyal to the Wang house and detested his conduct.

sentences.zh: 會鎔過匡威第慰忌辰，匡威縞衣裹甲，伏兵劫鎔入牙城。

translations.literal: When Rong passed Kuangwei's mansion to comfort him on the anniversary of a parent's death, Kuangwei wore mourning garb over armor and used hidden troops to seize Rong and carry him into the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong called at Kuangwei's mansion to observe the anniversary of a parent's death, Kuangwei wore mourning white over his armor and set ambush troops to seize Rong and drag him into the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 鎔兵逆戰，燔東偏門，軍士呼噪登屋，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: Rong's troops resisted; they burned the eastern side gate, soldiers shouted and climbed onto roofs, arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's troops fought back; they set fire to the eastern gate, soldiers shouted and scrambled onto the roofs, and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 鎔僕墨君和亂中扶鎔登屋免難，而斬匡威以徇。

translations.literal: Rong's servant Mo Junhe, amid the chaos, helped Rong up onto a roof to escape harm, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the chaos Rong's servant Mo Junhe helped him onto a roof to safety, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head.

sentences.zh: 是歲，匡籌出師攻鎮之樂壽、武強以報恥。

translations.literal: That year Kuangchou marched out to attack Lesou and Wuqiang in Zhen to avenge the humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: That year Kuangchou marched out to attack Lesou and Wuqiang in Zhen to avenge the insult.

sentences.zh: 匡威部曲劉仁恭歸於河東。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong, of Kuangwei's following, went over to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong, once of Kuangwei's command, went over to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 冬，河東聽仁恭之謀，出師進討。

translations.literal: In winter Hedong heeded Rengong's counsel and marched out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hedong took Rengong's advice and marched out to chastise Yan.

sentences.zh: 二月，敗燕軍於居庸，匡籌挈其族遁去，將赴京師。

translations.literal: In the second month they defeated the Yan army at Juyong; Kuangchou fled with his clan, intending to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they routed the Yan army at Juyong; Kuangchou fled with his clan, intending to reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 至景城，為滄州節度使盧彥威所殺，掠其輜車、妓妾。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingcheng he was killed by Military Governor Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou, who plundered his baggage train and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingcheng he was killed by Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, who plundered his baggage train and concubines.

sentences.zh: 匡籌妻張氏產於路，不能進，劉仁恭獲之，獻於李克用，後立為夫人，嬖寵專房。

translations.literal: Kuangchou's wife Lady Zhang gave birth on the road and could not proceed; Liu Rengong captured her and presented her to Li Keyong; she was later made his consort and enjoyed exclusive favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, Kuangchou's wife, gave birth on the road and could go no farther; Liu Rengong seized her and presented her to Li Keyong, who later made her his principal consort and favored her above all others.

sentences.zh: 李氏父子三葉，十年而亡。

translations.literal: The Li father and son for three generations — within ten years they were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Li father and son held power for three generations and were gone within ten years.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：大都偶國，亂之本也。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: When great cities rival the state, that is the root of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historiographer writes: When great cities rival the throne, disorder takes root.

sentences.zh: 故古先哲王建國，公侯之封，不過千乘，所以強幹弱枝，防其悖慢。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient sage-kings in founding states limited the enfeoffment of lords and marquises to no more than a thousand chariots, thereby strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches to guard against rebellion and insolence.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage-kings of old, in founding states, capped the fiefs of lords and marquises at a thousand chariots—strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches to forestall rebellion and insolence.

sentences.zh: 彼幽州者，列九圍之一，地方千里而遙，其民剛強，厥田沃壤。

translations.literal: That region of Youzhou is one of the nine frontier defense areas, a thousand li in extent and remote; its people are tough and its fields fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou is one of the nine frontier circuits, a thousand li across and far from the capital; its people are hard and its soil rich.

sentences.zh: 遠則慕田光、荊卿之義，近則染祿山、思明之風。

translations.literal: In distant ages they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were stained by the ways of An Lushan and Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: In distant times they looked up to the loyalty of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent memory they were stained by the example of An Lushan and Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 二百餘年，自相崇樹，雖朝廷有時命帥，而土人多務逐君。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years they honored each other in succession; though the court at times appointed commanders, the locals mostly strove to drive out their rulers.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two hundred years they raised up their own leaders in turn; though the court sometimes named a commander, the locals mostly worked to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 習苦忘非，尾大不掉，非一朝一夕之故也。

translations.literal: Accustomed to hardship, forgetting what is wrong, their tail too large to wag — this was not the work of a single morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Hardened by hardship, heedless of right and wrong, their tail grown too heavy to command—this did not happen overnight.

sentences.zh: 若李載義、張仲武、張允伸因利乘便，獲領旌旗，以仁守之，恭順朝旨，亦足多也。

translations.literal: Men such as Li Zaiyi, Zhang Zhongwu, and Zhang Yunshen, riding opportunity and convenience to gain the banners of command, governing with benevolence and respectfully following court directives — that too is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Li Zaiyi, Zhang Zhongwu, and Zhang Yunshen seized favorable moments to win the seals of command, then ruled with restraint and bowed to the court's will—that too deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 如硃克融、楊志誠、史元忠、張公素、李可舉、李全忠，以不仁得之，靡更曩志。

translations.literal: But Zhu Kerong, Yang Zhicheng, Shi Yuanzhong, Zhang Gongsu, Li Keju, and Li Quanzhong gained power without benevolence and never changed their former designs.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhu Kerong, Yang Zhicheng, Shi Yuanzhong, Zhang Gongsu, Li Keju, and Li Quanzhong won power without benevolence and never abandoned their old ambitions.

sentences.zh: 或尋為篡奪，或僅傳子孫，咸非令終，蓋其宜也。

translations.literal: Some were soon usurped, some passed power only to sons — none met a good end, as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Some were soon overthrown, some held on only long enough to pass power to a son—none died well, as was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蠍石之野，氣勁人豪。

translations.literal: Praise says: In the wilds of scorpion stone, the air is fierce and the men heroic.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: On the scorpion-stone frontier the air is harsh and the men are fierce.

sentences.zh: 二百餘載，自相尊高。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years they honored themselves.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two hundred years they made themselves masters.

sentences.zh: 載義、仲武，亦多忠勞。

translations.literal: Zaiyi and Zhongwu also showed much loyalty and effort.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi and Zhongwu, too, gave much loyal service.

sentences.zh: 餘因篡得，不仁何逃？

translations.literal: The rest seized power through usurpation — how could unkindness escape its due?
translations.idiomatic: The rest won power by usurpation—how could cruelty escape its reckoning?
